items.claim: The unit buries the book's primary macro-seam device mid-span at a junction the mark layer independently keys, leaves an in-span ketiv/qere undisclosed, and truncates its own frame splice below the gloss paired with it.
items.evidence: Word-event: the splice opens the verse with וַֽיְהִי֙ (oshb:Jer.37.6, byte) and is a confirmed member of the vayehi debar-YHWH shape; the three shapes are disjoint verse sets (sweep: 21 / 11 / 4 verses, no shared verse), so the shape label itself holds. But that onset is verse-initial at 37:6, i.e. INSIDE the span, and the mark inventory keys a petuchah to MT 37:5 - the junction immediately before it (single-witness WLC; tier-3 weak, never a driver; absence never counterevidence). Tier-1 device and tier-3 mark therefore converge on an interior junction at 37:5/37:6 while the unit is held at high confidence and the rival is disposed of on content grounds alone (same messengers), the petuchah being re-described as texture for the content of verse 5 rather than as the junction it keys. K/Q: the inventory records one note inside the span at MT 37:4, standing in the bytes as בֵּ֥ית הכליא הַכְּלֽוּא (oshb:Jer.37.4, byte; ketiv/qere pair, single-witness); no disclosure appears, although the note at MT 38:2 is disclosed in the material covering Jer.38.1-Jer.38.6, so this is an inconsistency rather than an absent convention. Quote/gloss parity: the frame splice ends on the construct אֱלֹהֵ֣י while the verse continues יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.37.7, byte), so the English supplying 'of Israel' has no counterpart in the Hebrew offered, and the declared elohei-yisrael signal is never quoted in full. Confirmed accurate: petuchah at MT 37:5 and setumah at MT 37:8 match under their correct types; paseq counts at MT 37:7 (1 seg) and MT 37:9 (1 seg) match the inventory and are correctly held count-only with no position claimed. Declared-flag dispositions confirmed: the never-blend statement is byte-true on the disjoint sets above, and the straight-quote flag lands on the WEB text's own second-level marks inside a run that does carry the mandated curly wrapper and inline ref.

items.claim: Every seam signal, mark citation, and name disambiguation in this unit verifies at the bytes, and the span owes no ketiv/qere or paseq disclosure.
items.evidence: Both pointed splices reach byte tier at their cited refs (oshb:Jer.37.11, oshb:Jer.37.16), as does בֶּן חֲנַנְיָ֑ה at oshb:Jer.37.13 (byte). The three-generation line יִרְאִיָּ֔יה בֶּן שֶֽׁלֶמְיָ֖ה בֶּן חֲנַנְיָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.37.13, byte) holds, and the Hananiah there is the captain's grandfather, distinct from the Hananiah of ch 28 - a per-site read, not a token sweep. Marks: setumah keyed to MT 37:11 and petuchah keyed to MT 37:16 both match the inventory under the correct types, PE and SAMEKH not conflated (single-witness WLC; tier-3 weak; absence never counterevidence), and the petuchah does key to the span's own end verse. Disclosure: no ketiv/qere note falls inside Jer.37.11-Jer.37.16 - the chapter's two notes sit at MT 37:4 and MT 37:19, both outside - and no paseq seg falls in the span, so nothing is owed and nothing is over-claimed. Name-form hazard is not live here: every Jeremiah occurrence in chs 37-38 carries the long spelling, the short spelling being confined to chs 27-29 (sweep: 8 verses), and the unit makes no spelling claim. One loose point, not carried: the setumah is called texture 'at the turn' where it in fact keys after 37:11 rather than at the 37:10/37:11 junction; the unit expressly disclaims it as warrant, so the seam does not rest on it. Declared-flag dispositions confirmed: the straight-quote flag falls on the WEB text's own inner marks inside a properly wrapped run, and the 'single chain' wording is not an exclusivity claim.

items.claim: The unit's substantive original-language work is byte-correct throughout, but it carries an undisclosed ketiv/qere note inside its own span.
items.evidence: K/Q: the inventory records one note inside Jer.37.17-Jer.37.21, at MT 37:19, standing in the bytes as ואיו וְאַיֵּה֙ (oshb:Jer.37.19, byte; ketiv/qere pair, single-witness). The unit discloses no ketiv/qere anywhere, while the note at MT 38:2 is disclosed in the material covering Jer.38.1-Jer.38.6 - so the omission is an inconsistency, not a convention the material lacks. Everything else verifies. The courtly reading is byte-correct and is the cluster's hardest call: אֲדֹנִ֣י (oshb:Jer.37.20, byte) carries hiriq under the nun (U+05B4), against qamats at the eleven divine-title sites (1:6, 2:19, 2:22, 4:10, 7:20, 14:13, 32:17, 32:25, 44:26, 49:5, 50:31), leaving exactly two courtly sites book-wide (37:20, 38:9); the unit names the pointing contrast rather than the consonants alone, and its forward cross-reference lands on the second of the two. Marks: the petuchah keyed to MT 37:16 does sit at this unit's front junction and the setumah keyed to MT 37:17 matches under its own type (single-witness WLC; tier-3 weak). Fold fidelity: web:Jer.37.17 is a continuation-fold site and the English is quoted against the staged folded reading, matching it including the lower-case onset. Declared-flag dispositions confirmed: both straight-quote flags fall on the WEB text's own second-level marks inside runs carrying the mandated curly wrapper and inline ref.

items.claim: The unit's stated name-disambiguation principle is refuted by the very bytes it splices, and both divine formulas standing in its span are left unquoted with the formula's mouth misassigned.
items.evidence: Name forms. The cistern owner at 38:6 is מַלְכִּיָּ֣הוּ בֶן הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ (oshb:Jer.38.6, byte) - the only -yahu form of that name in the book (sweep: 1 verse) - while the official's patronymic at 38:1 is מַלְכִּיָּ֑ה (oshb:Jer.38.1, byte), the -yah form (sweep: 4 name verses - 21:1, 25:18, 38:1, 46:25). Both are rendered by one English name with no spelling disclosure, at the exact site the campaign's per-attested-spelling rule targets. The claim that the bytes disambiguate each figure by full patronymic fails in both directions inside this material: 21:1 carries the identical Pashhur-plus-Malchiah pair, so the full patronymic joins rather than separates, and the ch-20 Pashhur the unit names instead is not the collision; conversely the embassy member at 37:3 is יְהוּכַ֣ל בֶּן שֶֽׁלֶמְיָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.37.3, byte; sweep: 1 verse for that name form) against וְיוּכַל֙ בֶּן שֶׁ֣לֶמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.38.1, byte), where both elements differ in form, so full-patronymic matching would split one man. That 38:1 name is additionally a consonantal homograph of the common verb, which stands inside this same span at 38:5 (sweep: 12 verses on that skeleton). Frame ownership. Two koh-amar frames fall in span - כֹּה֮ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ (oshb:Jer.38.2, byte) and כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.38.3, byte) - and neither is quoted; the splice offered begins after the formula, the sentence attached to it names Yahweh as the formula's mouth where 38:1's bytes make these the words Jeremiah was speaking to all the people, and the second frame at 38:3 goes unmentioned while the declared koh-amar signal rests on no quoted form. Confirmed accurate: setumah keyed to MT 38:1, MT 38:2 and MT 38:6 all match under the correct type (single-witness WLC; tier-3 weak), the last at the span's own end junction; and the ketiv/qere at MT 38:2 is disclosed and correctly scoped - the splice does end before the pair, which stands later in the verse. Declared-flag disposition REFUTED: the flagged sentence asserting that the bytes disambiguate each figure by full patronymic is not a heuristic false positive but a factual defect, on the 21:1 and 37:3 evidence above.

items.claim: The unit narrates the exact token that carries the span's only ketiv/qere note without disclosing the note, against the rule that pmark state is checked before any content claim in a K/Q verse.
items.evidence: K/Q: the inventory records one note inside Jer.38.7-Jer.38.13, at MT 38:11, standing in the bytes as בְּלוֹיֵ֣ הסחבות סְחָב֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.38.11, byte; ketiv/qere pair, single-witness). The rag-and-cord sentence characterizes precisely that word, and the unit discloses no ketiv/qere; the parallel word one verse later is plain pointed text, בְּלוֹאֵ֨י הַסְּחָב֤וֹת (oshb:Jer.38.12, byte), so the variant is specific to the verse the prose leans on. The note at MT 38:2 is disclosed in the material covering Jer.38.1-Jer.38.6, so the convention is present in this material and simply not applied here. Lesser observation: the Cushite epithet is carried at 38:7, 38:10 and 38:12 but dropped at 38:11, where the bytes read עֶֽבֶד מֶ֨לֶךְ alone (oshb:Jer.38.11, byte) - a per-site naming variation inside the span that the continuity note does not touch. Confirmed accurate: the courtly reading at 38:9 is byte-correct - אֲדֹנִ֣י (oshb:Jer.38.9, byte) carries hiriq under the nun, the second and last of the book's two courtly sites against eleven divine qamats sites, and the unit names the pointing rather than the consonants. Setumah keyed to MT 38:6 and MT 38:13 matches under the correct type at both of the unit's junctions (single-witness WLC; tier-3 weak). All three pointed splices reach byte tier at their cited refs, and no fold site is quoted. items.claim: The divine-title claim at 38:17 has no support in the form the unit quotes, blends distinct count objects, and asserts an in-chapter recurrence the bytes do not contain; a cited K/Q verse is also left undisclosed.
items.evidence: The quoted run צִדְקִיָּ֡הוּ כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֩ (oshb:Jer.38.17, byte) stops before any title: the stack it is said to carry stands next in the verse as אֱלֹהֵ֨י צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Jer.38.17, byte), and the run's first word is the addressee's name, not part of a title - so the English gloss paired with it has no counterpart in the Hebrew offered, which is a mandatory-engagement failure on a boundary-relevant title claim, not a wording matter. The object is blended. This is the Elohei-tsevaot Elohei-Yisrael form (sweep: 3 verses - 35:17, 38:17, 44:7; the YHWH Elohei-tsevaot shape is 5 verses - 5:14, 15:16, 35:17, 38:17, 44:7), a different count object from the book's signature stack YHWH tsevaot Elohei Yisrael (sweep: 32 verses), of which 38:17 is NOT a member, and from the YHWH-tsevaot object. The recurrence claim is false at the bytes: of the 3 verses carrying that form book-wide, exactly 1 falls in chs 37-38, namely 38:17 itself (sweep: 3 verses, 1 in chs 37-38), so the assertion that the same full stack is used elsewhere in these chapters has no site to point to, and it is made with no digit and no sweep - a tier label on the splice does not stand in for the recurrence check. K/Q: the inventory records a note at MT 38:16 - a verse this unit cites for its mark and characterizes as the king's sworn oath - with the pair standing inside that oath clause, חַי יְהוָ֞ה את אֲשֶׁר֩ (oshb:Jer.38.16, byte; single-witness); no disclosure appears. Confirmed accurate: setumah keyed to MT 38:13, MT 38:16, MT 38:18 and petuchah keyed to MT 38:19 all match the inventory under their own types, never conflated (single-witness WLC; tier-3 weak); the 38:14 splice reaches byte tier; and the oracle's mouth is correctly named as Jeremiah's rather than left to the formula. The unit's closing junction at 38:20/38:21 is the contested seam treated under Jer.38.21-Jer.38.23. Declared-flag disposition confirmed: the straight-quote flag falls on the WEB text's own inner marks inside a properly wrapped run.

items.claim: The unit's front seam cuts inside one unbroken speech turn, and the showing-formula warrant offered for the cut is contradicted by the bytes and withdrawn by the unit's own device note.
items.evidence: The last speech introduction before the seam is וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ (oshb:Jer.38.20, byte); 38:21 then opens וְאִם מָאֵ֥ן אַתָּ֖ה לָצֵ֑את (oshb:Jer.38.21, byte) with no speech formula, no addressee change, no narrative frame and no dated notice - a waw-conditional resuming the conditional series already running inside that same turn at אִם יָצֹ֨א תֵצֵ֜א (oshb:Jer.38.17, byte) and וְאִ֣ם לֹֽא תֵצֵ֗א (oshb:Jer.38.18, byte). The verse runs to nine words in total, quoted here but for its closing divine name, so the account is exhaustive: nothing in the pointed text marks a new unit onset at 38:21. The showing formula does not carry the seam either: הִרְאַ֖נִי (oshb:Jer.38.21, byte) stands in exactly two verses (sweep: 2 verses - 24:1, 38:21), so the device note's plural reference to the book's formal vision reports overstates a form with one other site and carries no digit; and the same note concedes the showing is embedded inside an ongoing address rather than standing as a separate report, which withdraws the only warrant offered for the cut. An embedded formula is precisely the case where the mouth and the nesting decide, and here both run continuously from 38:20. The mark layer offers no corroboration at this junction - petuchah keys to MT 38:19 and MT 38:23, not to 38:20 (single-witness WLC; tier-3 weak, and absence is never counterevidence, so this is stated as non-corroboration only). Confirmed accurate: the petuchah keyed to MT 38:23 does sit at the unit's closing junction; both pointed splices reach byte tier at their cited refs; and no ketiv/qere note falls in Jer.38.21-Jer.38.23. Lesser point: the poetic-lines characterization of 38:22 rests on the modern line layout of the English rather than on any pointed-text signal, and carries no tier label. Declared-flag disposition confirmed: the straight-quote flag falls on the WEB text's own inner marks inside a properly wrapped run.

items.claim: The closing splice runs past the English it is paired with, and the clause it adds is a temporal protasis left open across the unit's own closing seam without disclosure.
items.evidence: Quote/gloss parity: the closing splice ends with וְהָיָ֕ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר נִלְכְּדָ֖ה יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:Jer.38.28, byte), while the rendering at web:Jer.38.28 it is said to match stops at the taking of the city and carries no counterpart for that clause - so quote and gloss are not parallel and a real witness divergence at the unit's own end verse goes undisclosed. Cross-seam cohesion: that clause is a temporal protasis with no main clause following it inside the span; the dating notices at MT 39:1-2 intervene and the narrative main clause follows at וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ (oshb:Jer.39.3, byte). A byte-true construction straddling the unit's own closing junction argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed, and the unit instead reads the verse as a clean custodial close at high confidence. Confirmed accurate, and this unit's mark handling is the most complete in this material: petuchah keyed to MT 38:26 and MT 38:27 and the doubled setumah-plus-petuchah keyed to MT 38:28 all match the inventory, the doubled verse being the only two-type verse among the 16 marked verses in Jer.37.3-Jer.38.28 (sweep: 1 of 16) and explicitly not conflated (single-witness WLC; tier-3 weak); the front junction's petuchah at MT 38:23 is likewise correct. No ketiv/qere note falls in Jer.38.24-Jer.38.28, so none is owed, and both pointed splices reach byte tier. Declared-flag dispositions confirmed: the never-conflated wording is a disclosure disclaimer that the doubled mark at MT 38:28 bears out, and the 'continuous' wording is not an exclusivity claim.
